data_sources.name: Integrated Values Survey (IVS): World Values Survey (WVS) and European Values Study (EVS) trend file; waves 2005–2009, 2011–2013, 2017–2020 (plus earlier waves 1990–1992, 1999–2000 for appendix figures)
Comparative Manifesto Project (CMP / Manifesto Project), incl. manifesto text (Merz et al. 2016) and DeepL translations
The PopuList (Rooduijn et al. 2024) – classification of populist radical right parties
Party leader demographics hand-collected from Wikipedia pages; log weekly wage by occupation from IPUMS 2023
Share of female legislators: Weeks et al. 2023 (Männerparteien); Adams, Bracken, Gidron, Horne, O'Brien, Senk 2023; Global Legislator Database 2024
Party Facts (Döring and Regel 2019) – linking CMP and IVS parties
ParlGov – governing coalition status (used to drop opinion variables affected by coalition status)
German Politbarometer (Forschungsgruppe Wahlen) – 'most important issue' question, Germany case study
Perspective API (insult attribute) applied to manifesto clauses; Comparative Agendas Project, Polidoc, Manifesto Vault (supplementary manifesto texts)
GPT-4o classification of manifesto clauses as pledges vs declarative statements
Ipsos 2009 aggregate polling (UKIP/BNP support, cited as external check)

data_processing_steps.description: Classify parties as populist radical right (PRRP) if the PopuList ever classified them as PRRP since 2005. Other party families (center-left = social democratic; center-right = Christian democratic/conservative; green = ecological; socialist) are assigned from CMP party family codes.

Party positions: all 56 CMP main (three-digit) variables. Economic index (19 positions, free market vs government intervention) and cultural/'society' index (11 positions, conservative vs progressive) from CMP; conservative positions added, liberal subtracted. Alternative indices (Bakker-Hobolt, Prosser, expanded Hawk-Dove, European integration, government efficiency) used in robustness.

Leadership demographics hand-coded for party-election observations: gender, years of schooling, age, marital status, number of divorces, minority status (immigrant, non-Christian, non-white, or non-heterosexual), log average weekly wage of leader's previous occupation (IPUMS 2023); share of female legislators merged from three sources by CMP ID/Parlgov ID with closest-year match within 5 years. Missing leader demographics imputed with random forests.

Manifesto rhetoric: lexical diversity (MATTR, 200-word window, stopwords removed), average words per clause, total word count, and insult score (mean Perspective API insult score of the top 5% most insulting clauses, after DeepL translation to English). Missing/PDF-only manifestos supplemented from CAP, Polidoc, Manifesto Vault; four pairs imputed with random forests. Split-half consistency test (odd vs even sections).

Pledge-based positions: GPT-4o classifies manifesto clauses as pledges (1) or not (0); positions recomputed from pledges only; imputation by random forests for manifestos lacking annotated text; manual check of 100 clauses gave 98% agreement.

Voter data: IVS waves 2005–2009, 2011–2013 (7 countries: Estonia, Germany, Netherlands, Poland, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden), 2017–2020; 20 European countries (Austria, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UK), requiring ≥70% of voters supporting a CMP-matchable party and ≥50% supporting parties existing in first and last waves. Over 100 demographic and opinion variables; excludes left-right self-placement (used as alternative outcome), confidence in parliament/parties/government (affected by coalition status), and a priorities question. Missing values imputed by random forests per country-wave (or by interpolation across waves). Weights: IVS sampling weights, normalized so each country (and each survey within country-wave) has equal weight.
variables_involved: preferred party (vote intention or party appealing most)

data_processing_steps.description: Merge IVS and CMP via Party Facts (manual linking otherwise); assign party positions from election closest to mean survey date; drop respondents without CMP data within ±5 years and those supporting parties with <10 respondents. Parties defined by CMP ID.

PRRP score: LASSO regression predicting PRRP support in 2017–2020 from all IVS opinion variables (country indicators unpenalized and excluded when computing score); standardized fitted value predicted for voters in all waves.

Opinion indices for reduced-form analysis: economic and cultural opinion indices from IVS variables resembling CMP index components, loadings from first principal component on pooled 2005–2009 and 2017–2020 data; left-right self-identification (1–10) regressed nonparametrically on the two indices by wave.

Step 1 estimation: multinomial logit utility U_ij = x_i'Φ z_j + δ_j + ε_ij, estimated separately per wave by penalized MLE with nuclear-norm penalty on Φ (proximal gradient descent; λ by cross-validation). Step 2: δ differences regressed on average party characteristics and their changes (Oaxaca-type), with β restricted to span of first k=5 right singular vectors of Φ (k=3, 7 in robustness), linear trend in β using 2011–2013 wave, weighted by party vote share, country-by-wave fixed effects; residual ζ recovered from δ.

Four-component decomposition of change in PRRP support 2005–2009 to 2017–2020 (priorities, attributes, party characteristics, residual) per country; order: priorities, attributes, party characteristics, residual last (ζ = −∞ for non-existent parties). Aggregated across countries with weights equal to inverse of 2017–2020 PRRP support share; total scaled to 100%; countries not in 2011–2013 wave imputed by average. 200 bootstrap replications resampling voters within wave.

Robustness variants: Shorrocks-Shapley average over six component orders; leave-country-out; bliss-point model (quadratic party characteristics, k=3); age replaced by cohort; added rhetoric variables; pledges-only positions; separate estimation for higher-income (Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, UK) and lower-income countries (Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain); without demographics; k=3 and k=7; adding Czech Republic and Slovakia; dropping Greece and Italy.

Weights analysis: voter weights w_i = x_i'Φ + β; aggregated into economic/cultural index weights (average of position weights, sign-flipped for left-wing positions); distribution compared across waves holding attributes at 2017–2020; heterogeneity by subgroup (age, sex, college, income, urban, union, PRRP score) of priority-driven PRRP increase and of change in log |w_culture|/|w_econ|.

Spatial counterfactual: predicted PRRP (National Front/AfD) support in each country in 2017–2020 using French (German) party set, characteristics and residuals and estimated priorities, varying only the country's voter attribute distribution; U.S. added with one EU question imputed.

Residual decomposition into new PRRP entrants vs existing PRRP; latent demand for new parties in 2005–2009 using 2017–2020 residuals or residuals imputed from a regression on country and party-family fixed effects.

Cross-country similarity test: for each party with >50 supporters, linear probability model of support on voter attributes within its country; correlate fitted values across party pairs from different countries and average by party family. Shy-voter check: LASSO multinomial logit predicting party support for undecided respondents.

tables.label: Table 1 (tab:sum_stat)
tables.title: Descriptive Statistics
tables.sample_restriction: Panel A: party characteristics (CMP economic and cultural indices, five positions that most distinguish PRRP from non-PRRP, leadership demographics incl. education, divorces, female legislator share), averages for 2005–2009 and 2017–2020 waves, PRRP vs non-PRRP, equal country weights and vote-share weights within country. Panel B: voter attributes from IVS (five key demographics incl. male, urban (city >100,000), plus five opinions with largest PRRP/non-PRRP difference, in SD units), IVS sampling weights within countries, countries equally weighted.
